decisions.text: each value minus its budget (budget): a deviation, sorted by the deviation, the budget itself the zero line; the unit says so (“over budget”) (G8.16)
the dividing value is 0, the budget itself: over budget is bad (G0.20)
a calculated value in place of the raw one: the deviation (G8.15)
type bar: categories compared by value
values on both sides of zero: room at both ends
nominal categories sorted by value, descending
every name fits under its bar, neighbours at least 10 pt apart: vertical bars
5 values against 7 scale labels: whichever puts fewer numbers on the chart (G2.18): the values labelled directly, the value scale and its gridlines removed, the zero line kept as the baseline
value labels as a set, one magnitude and one number of decimals, the prefix and suffix on each: +$36K, +$35K, +$12K, +$5K, −$9K (G6.16, G7.4)
the plot is pulled in by 2.6 pt so that the outer names stay inside the figure
every label just outside its bar's end: neither the text grey nor white reads on the bar's colour at 4.5 : 1 (G7.4, G6.5)
the unit's description on its own line above the plot: “over budget”; the labels carry its prefix, suffix and magnitude
good and bad coloured by the dividing value, 0 (lower is good): bad Operations, Marketing, R&D, IT; good Finance & Admin (G4.16)

static output, in colour: one file, red for bad and green for good, plain, for every reader (D-18; owner, 1 Oct 2026); black and white (audience.bw_risk) adds the textures, and a style may choose the colour-blind-safe pair (--good-bad-mode: safe-pair)

source.shows: one view of a spray-and-pray set, titled with the question it answers (RP5-5, RP5-6): expenses minus budget, over budget bad and under budget good, in red and green (G4.16, D-18); the merged set is builder D's
